jobs.name: Self-improvement review loop
jobs.description: Frequent autonomous review of learnings, errors, and feature requests with low-risk promotion.

payload.message:
Review the workspace self-improvement logs for the last day and identify repeated failures, corrections, and feature requests.

Tasks:
- summarize new items since the last review
- cluster repeated issues by pattern
- suggest the smallest durable fix for each repeated pattern
- identify anything that should be promoted to AGENTS.md, TOOLS.md, SOUL.md, or MEMORY.md
- if a low-risk item is repeated and non-sensitive, auto-promote the minimal durable edit instead of only suggesting it

Autopromotion policy:
- safe to auto-promote: documentation, wording, checklists, routing hints, tooling notes, and other non-sensitive workflow clarifications
- do not auto-promote: anything involving secrets, credentials, permissions, external actions, safety policy changes, or user-private content
- if uncertain, stage the suggestion and explain why it was not auto-applied

Constraints:
- do not expose secrets or raw transcripts
- prefer short bullet points
- keep the output actionable

Use the self-improvement routine in `SELF_IMPROVEMENT_ROUTINE.md` as the operating guide.

jobs.name: Daily model utilisation and effectiveness check
jobs.description: Daily review of recent OpenClaw usage with live session and cron coverage checks.

payload.message:
Review the last 24 hours of OpenClaw activity for manager-bot and any other sessions visible in the manager tree. Summarize model utilisation, token usage, error rate, retries, and any signs that the current default model (`openai/gpt-5.4-mini`) is underpowered for the workload.

Add a separate section titled `Utilisation vs Efficiency` with:
- total usage and where it concentrated
- whether the same work could be done with fewer tokens or fewer retries
- signs of wasted context, overlong prompts, or avoidable escalation
- a clear call on whether we should keep the current default or dial up to `GPT_FULL`

Add a `Coverage` section that explicitly says:
- how many visible sessions were included
- whether any live session is still running at the time of the report
- whether any cron job was still in progress or pending
- whether visibility is restricted to the manager tree, and what that means for confidence

Use `openclaw session status` for the current session and `openclaw cron status/list` to capture live state. Separate finished runs from in-progress work. If you see repeated failures, long contexts, or obvious quality issues, recommend whether we should dial up to `GPT_FULL` or keep the current default. Post a concise report with findings, the separate `Utilisation vs Efficiency` section, the `Coverage` section, a recommendation, and any blockers. Do not expose secrets or raw transcripts.
